items_missed: Never asked 'How are you today?' — opened straight into the quote request
No agenda statement with a rough timeframe — said 'let me get a few details and then I can work up that quote' but never framed how long the call would take
No Worries Damage Coverage ($2,000) never mentioned
No full 'no hidden fees' pitch — listed the extra charges but never the no credit card fee / no fuel surcharge / no transportation fee framing

Zero Save Your Ass content — no 'prep shortens the move and lowers the bill', no consolidation examples, no carload tip. This was the highest-leverage miss on the call: the customer said the quote was over budget and that one bedroom was already packed, which was a wide-open invitation for the prep speech
No attempt to book — customer said 'let me call you back' and the rep replied 'okay, sounds good' with no ask for the schedule, no availability urgency, and no follow-up commitment or callback time
Never mentioned that no deposit is required
No 'reply with any corrections', no bolded detail list at the top of the email, no 'any other questions before I let you go?', no hours or how to reach us
Used the customer's name essentially once (garbled) across a 10-minute call
No Ecobox referral despite a budget-constrained customer facing a $220 packing-materials line and saying 'I just hate packing'
No insurance explanation (No Worries or 60¢/lb) — 'insurance' was named only as an item in the included list
Traffic never mentioned as a variable on a 25-minute cross-Houston drive
top_strength: The discovery was the best part of this call and close to textbook — origin and destination both confirmed, square footage, floor levels at both ends, walk distance at both ends, storage/garage, heavy and fragile items, appliances, workout equipment, antiques, additional stops, box count benchmarked against a two-bedroom norm, and an explicit stressor question. The clock explanation was also complete and clean: on-site start, contract signed on arrival, 2.5-hour minimum, 15-minute increments, then 'any questions there?'
coaching_note: Joel gathered everything and then gave the price away with no close. When the customer said $1,200-$1,400 was over budget, the answer was a smaller number — it should have been the Save Your Ass prep speech plus a partial-pack option and an Ecobox referral, then an ask for the schedule. Never end a quote call with 'okay, sounds good' — always attempt the booking and set a specific callback.
phone_presence_notes: Polite, organized, and easy to follow, but transactional — almost no name use, and when the customer voiced budget stress and said she hates packing, the response was 'mm-hmm alright, makes sense' rather than any real empathy or rapport.
